tables.heading: CLI protocol, version 1
rows: Runs the engine in the foreground (start mode `standalone`); with `--detach` it makes a run request of kind `engine`. It continues an unfinished run of the feature and takes `--new-run` and `--reset-counts`, as `launch` does. It takes the ported flags of the baseline, among them `--telemetry`, `--loki-url`, `--otel`, `--otel-url` and `-j`; their keys and the rule that combines them are §K.10 of feature 110
Runs the launch checks, writes the launch record, starts the runtime root, waits for the handshake. `--dry-run` withholds the launch. `--new-run` starts a new run

Continues a run from the records on disk. `--reset-counts` resets counts. `--accept-source-change` accepts an intended change of spec, plan or task list. `--resolve-roles` asks for a new resolution of roles, on `resume` and on `launch`. A run that was launched through the runtime root is continued through the runtime root
Writes the stop request. `--now` ends owned processes. `--jobs` also ends adoptable jobs
Prints the state of the run from the read model: text, `--line`, `--json`
With `--until-change`: prints nothing while nothing changes; prints and takes the cursor
Inspection commands, each with a byte cap
Learning: show, advise, apply, revert, evaluate
The spec module as a public command
The verification plan and the verification gate as a public command
Reverse specification. `--detach` makes a run request of kind `engine`; `--comment` takes the consumer's comment
The launch-contract commands: derive (with the judgment exchange of §G.9), validate, promote, render
From sources to a promoted launch contract and a launcher. The spelling of the commands is the owner's
The pipeline entry in the foreground. `--dry-run` prints the plan
Readers of a run, and `relaunch` with `relaunch.owner: supervise`. `supervise hold` and `supervise release` write and lift the inbox request `hold-relaunch`
Writes an inbox request of type `host-event` on behalf of a host
113 for the caller; 122 for the inbox
Runs the registered checks. With the launch checks only, it evaluates them without launching, for a host hook
Move or take over the control plane of a feature

Runs the conformance suite on a harness, on request, inside a budget that is an argument of the command. The command belongs to 109; the state of the harness that results belongs to 146. The registry queries of the baseline are internal operations with result records and are no commands
The resolved configuration with its sources; the schema

Always, unless compatibility output is selected
The lines of the baselines byte for byte, artefacts of the old languages included, and no other line
Selected by configuration (`output.compat`); always under the `parity` profile

The pipeline entry and the runtime root

`supervise`; with `relaunch.owner: root` the compatibility projection of the root's events

With the layer on: `strategy`, `level`, `containment`, `protection`, `units`, `pass`, `fail`, `unchecked`, `tainted`, `cycles`, `disengaged`, `escalations`, `failfast-stops`, `fallback`. The value of `protection` is `prevent`, `detect`, or `detect,basic` where only the basic protection holds. With the layer off: `strategy=classic reason=<reason>`. Only with parallel units on, also: `parallel`, `workers`, `groups`, `group-failures`, `refused`, `worker-caches`, `wall-hours`, `agent-hours`, and the fallback reason
Pairs `key=value` separated by one space. A text value is quoted as in JSON
Pairs `key=value` separated by one space, starting with `run=` and `st=`; with `validUntil=` where it is precomputed
As at the baseline. A prefix that named an implementation file is replaced by a logical component name

Records each answer with its provenance (who answered, through which harness) in the launch contract and in the digest
